info.title: Inth API
info.description: Inth consent and legal document API

get.description: The consent policy for this visitor, the banner text, and the policy snapshot token a save sends back. A browser sends its inputs as the query parameters below, so the request stays simple and needs no preflight. An app may send them as the headers `x-inth-country`, `x-inth-region`, `x-inth-gpc`, `x-inth-experiment` and `x-inth-vendors` instead. A query parameter wins over its header.
get.summary: Resolve the consent policy for this visitor

parameters.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the visitor.
parameters.name: country

parameters.description: ISO 3166-2 subdivision code of the visitor.
parameters.name: region

parameters.description: A banner experiment arm to show.

get.description: The project’s policy set, the same for every visitor, so it may be cached and resolved on a server. Answers with an `ETag`; send it back as `If-None-Match` for a `304` when nothing changed. `language` asks for the banner text in one language only.

parameters.description: Only the banner text in this language.
parameters.name: language

post.description: Saves a banner answer for a subject and property, merged with the answer already stored: for each category, the receipt confirmed later wins, and a category left out keeps what is stored. A retry with the same idempotencyKey is recorded once and answered as the first try was. With externalId and an identityToken that names it, the subject is linked to that person. An identity never fails a save: `link` says whether the link was stored.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

parameters.description: The ID of the visit’s consent journey, made by the SDK.
parameters.name: journey

parameters.description: How long the journey lasts: one page, or the tab.
parameters.name: journeyScope

post.description: Sent by a server that rendered a visit from a cached manifest. Send the IP address of the visitor on `x-inth-client-ip`, and their user agent on `user-agent`. A request from a page, which sends `Origin`, is refused. Nothing is stored.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

post.summary: Report a visit resolved from a cached manifest

post.description: Links a device to a person, by your account ID for them. Needs the secret key, or an identityToken in the body that names externalId. Makes the device subject when it does not exist yet. A link the device already has writes nothing, so a retry is safe.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

post.summary: Link a device to a person

parameters.description: A lower-case UUIDv7 the SDK makes. A legacy `sub_` ID is accepted too; the answer names the subject’s UUID, to store in its place.
parameters.name: id

post.description: Signs a token, valid for an hour, that lets a browser act for one person: link its device, or record their acceptance. Needs the secret key. Make one per sign-in or page load, and do not store it. Nothing is stored.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

put.description: Publishes a release of a legal document and makes it the one in force for its type. `requiresAcceptance` defaults to true; false marks a small edit, which people who accepted the release before it are not asked to accept again. Publishing a release the project already has, with the same version, effective date and requiresAcceptance, makes it current again. A hash already published under another version, or a version with another hash, is a conflict.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

parameters.description: A document type, such as `terms_us` or `privacy_policy`.
parameters.name: type

get.description: The release of a legal document in force for its type. Send its `hash` back with an acceptance to name the release that was shown.
get.summary: Read the legal document release in force

parameters.description: A document type, such as `terms_us` or `privacy_policy`.
parameters.name: type

post.description: Records that a device or a person accepted one or more legal document releases, each named by its type and the hash `GET /v1/documents/{type}/current` gave. A release no longer in force can still be accepted; `GET /v1/documents/check` then reports the newer one as not accepted. All are recorded, or none. With only subjectId, the acceptances are the device’s and need no key. With externalId, they are the person’s, who is made when missing, and the request needs the secret key or an identityToken that names them. `context` carries the visitor’s IP address and user agent when your server records the acceptance, and is read only with the secret key; otherwise both come from the request. A retry with the same idempotencyKey is recorded once and answered as the first try was.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

get.description: For a person, by your account ID for them, and each document type asked for: accepted when they accepted any release, and acceptedLatest when they accepted the latest release that requires acceptance, or one after it. Acceptances from devices linked to the person count. Every type asked for is in the answer.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

parameters.description: Your account ID for the person.
parameters.name: externalId

files.description: Files loaders download at run time, by the exact vendor URL a loader requests. `null`: the registry has no release of the file it may serve, so load it from nowhere.

sources.description: By script ID. `null`: the registry blocks the script, so load it from neither the registry nor the vendor. A script not listed loads from its vendor.

unavailable.description: The registry could not be read, so this answer says nothing about the scripts. Keep the list from an earlier answer.

ScriptRegistry.description: The Script Registry scripts to load by hash. Absent when the registry lists no script for the project.

integrity.description: The SRI hash of the file.

src.description: The registry copy of the release the loader is bound to.

ScriptRegistryFile.description: Where to load one file a loader downloads at run time.

attributes.description: Attributes to set on the script tag, for a script that reads its own URL. Skip one the page already sets. Remove an attribute whose value is `null`.

integrity.description: The SRI hash of the version. Load it with `crossorigin="anonymous"`.

refuseIfSet.description: On a loader that downloads more files at run time: integration options, by dotted path, with which it would download them from an address `files` does not list. With any of them set, load nothing for the script.

src.description: The URL of the version the registry serves, named by its hash. Keep its query string.
